backs: Track B go/no-go: re-pointing benchmarks/enterprise_rag.py at recall.reasoning.reason() does not face mass abstention. The _UNCALIBRATED 0.50 dense floor would drop AT LEAST 5.6% of the 500 questions.

The constraint on any post-rerank evidence gate: the loss is CONCENTRATED in miscellaneous (60% of its questions below the floor) which already scores 100.0 correctness, so a 0.50 dense gate there is a pure regression.

The other half of the go/no-go: dense_floor_summary.unanswerable_below_floor records 0 of 10 sampled info_not_found questions below the floor, so at 0.50 it pays 16% of the sample and abstains on none of the unanswerable ones.

_provenance.note:
Dense-cosine floor probe, NOT a retrieval quality measurement. Answers one question: how many questions would the trust layer's uncalibrated 0.50 threshold demote to low_confidence when the benchmark stops calling HybridRetriever.search() directly and goes through reason(). 

LOWER BOUND, not an estimate. best_dense_score is the corpus-wide dense top-1, while the trust floor is applied per RETURNED hit over the post-fusion post-rerank top-k. Since max(dense over the returned k) <= corpus top-1, a question counted safe here can still have no returned hit above the floor. The true demotion rate is at least this one. 

THREE DENOMINATORS, do not mix them. dense_floor_summary counts 16 of 100, over every sampled row. threshold_metrics['0.5'] reports 0.1375 over the 80 rows carrying expected_docs, which EXCLUDES all 10 high_level and all 10 info_not_found rows; since high_level is the second worst category, its 5 demotions sit outside that figure entirely. The 5.6% is over the 500-question population after reweighting. 

Reranker and SPLADE are deliberately OFF: best_dense_score is an independent call in retrieval_calibration and does not derive from hits, so the dense figures are identical to the submitted configuration while this run's 100 voyage:rerank-2.5 calls are not paid for. doc_ids_by_k and k_metrics therefore do NOT describe the submitted arm and must not be read as recall. 

Sample is stratified 10-per-category, which OVERWEIGHTS small categories: the 16% sample rate is not the population rate, 5.6% is. n=10 per category, so per-category rates have wide intervals (6/10 is Wilson [0.31, 0.83]); the direction is solid, the magnitude is not. 

⚠️ Re-running --calibrate-retrieval-out to THIS path overwrites the file. The runner now derives dense_floor_summary itself, but _provenance is hand-stamped and nothing regenerates it. Write a re-run somewhere else.
